query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause: quality of cabin crew service plausibly drives overall rating and recommendation. It is a manipulable factor SIA could improve, functioning as the treatment/driver being attributed.

per_column.name: food_quality_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Type of food-related failure is a candidate cause of dissatisfaction and non-recommendation; another driver rather than a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: special_meal_service_failure
per_column.rationale: A specific service failure that plausibly lowers rating; a candidate cause, not a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: service_amenity_reduction
per_column.rationale: Reduction of amenities is a candidate driver of lower ratings; a treatment-type factor.

per_column.name: cabin_class_value_gap
per_column.rationale: Perceived value gap sits on the causal path between service/product delivery and overall rating; it is a perception outcome largely determined by the other service factors, so adjusting for it as a confounder would be an error.

per_column.name: service_consistency_decline
per_column.rationale: Decline in consistency is a candidate cause of lower ratings; a driver, not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: loyalty_program_friction
per_column.rationale: Friction in loyalty program is a candidate driver of dissatisfaction; a treatment-type factor.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply many candidate CAUSES (treatments/drivers) of the outcome, but they do NOT supply any CONFOUNDERS -- variables that plausibly cause BOTH a treatment and the outcome and must be adjusted for to avoid biased attribution. Genuine confounders here would be things like traveller type, cabin class, route/region, or time period (many of which already exist in the original table but were not surfaced as adjustment variables). One column (cabin_class_value_gap) is a mediator on the causal path and would be an error to treat as a confounder. Because the technical claim requires (a) a treatment AND (b) surfaced confounders, and only (a) is satisfied, the causal-attribution setup is incomplete: effects estimated from these columns would be unadjusted and potentially biased.
